bull.b: Large, multi-year contracts with AMD and a frontier AI lab provide Riot with a durable avenue beyond Bitcoin mining. The 1,151 MW portfolio and approximately $38 billion of contracted revenue can improve business visibility and establish a substantial infrastructure platform as projects reach service.

The contracted lease portfolio is expected to produce substantial net operating income and attractive project-level returns once fully deployed. These economics could support stronger and more predictable cash generation than mining, while enabling reinvestment in additional infrastructure without relying solely on Bitcoin prices.

Low net electricity costs are strategically important because power is a core input to Bitcoin mining and a major determinant of competitiveness. Riot’s reported power credits and low net cost indicate an operating platform that can better withstand mining economics pressure and preserve flexibility across its sites.

bear.b: Riot is currently consuming cash while generating deeply negative earnings, which weakens internal funding capacity and reduces capital-allocation flexibility. Although contracted data-center projects may improve the mix over time, the present cost structure and losses create meaningful execution and financing pressure.

Bitcoin remains a material source of operating exposure, so weaker cryptocurrency prices can pressure revenue even when production increases. Ongoing sales also reduce the treasury cushion, leaving results and available funding more dependent on mining economics, project execution, and external financing.

The data-center strategy requires substantial capital before the contracted revenue ramp is fully realized. Tighter credit conditions, pending financings, and remaining Rockdale exposure to scope, site conditions, and owner-furnished equipment could increase funding needs or delay the expected improvement in cash generation.
